posts.topic: Write a useful portfolio case study
slides: MAKE YOUR PORTFOLIO SHOW PROOF
Explain the problem, your decisions and what you built.
Show the thinking behind the work.
creator presenting a laptop project and open case-study notebook
START WITH THE REAL PROBLEM
Who needed help? What task was difficult before?
Give the project useful context.
creator pointing to a small user card beside tangled task blocks
EXPLAIN YOUR ROLE CLEARLY
State what you owned and what others contributed.
Be specific about your contribution.
creator holding one orange work card among blue team cards
SHOW YOUR KEY DECISIONS
Explain one trade-off and why you chose that approach.
Make your reasoning visible.
creator weighing two project cards on a small balance
USE HONEST EVIDENCE
Show a demo, test result or feedback. Label unmeasured outcomes.
Evidence beats inflated claims.
creator showing a laptop demo beside feedback and test icons
WRITE ONE CASE STUDY TODAY
Use problem, process, result and next improvement.
Save this + document one project.

posts.topic: Build a simple freelance lead tracker
slides: STOP LOSING FREELANCE LEADS
Keep every enquiry and next action in one tracker.
Make follow-ups easy to find.
creator gathering orange enquiry cards into a blue tracker tray
CAPTURE THE USEFUL DETAILS
Add the contact, need, source and date of enquiry.
Record enough to follow up well.
creator filling a neat tracker sheet beside contact cards
USE A CLEAR LEAD STATUS
Try new, contacted, proposal sent, won and closed.
Know where each conversation stands.
creator arranging five coloured status cards on a small board
SET ONE NEXT ACTION
Add a follow-up date and a specific next step.
Turn the tracker into action.
creator placing a calendar icon and arrow beside one lead card
FOLLOW UP WITH CONTEXT
Address the client's need. Keep your message relevant and respectful.
Help the client make a decision.
creator sending a thoughtful message from laptop beside a proposal
REVIEW YOUR TRACKER WEEKLY

posts.topic: Ask for feedback that improves your work
slides: ASK FOR BETTER FEEDBACK
Show one clear goal and ask a focused question.
Make feedback useful.
creator holding a blue question card beside an orange project model
CHOOSE THE RIGHT REVIEWER
Ask someone who understands the task or represents the user.
Relevant feedback helps more.

SHOW A SPECIFIC PIECE OF WORK

ASK ABOUT ONE MAIN ISSUE
